extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, Central Reexamination Unit staff, patent practitioners and requesters involved in ex parte reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for deciding whether to order an ex parte reexamination of a U.S. patent, including statutory/claim-construction standards, timing, required content of requests, treatment of prior art and court/Office decisions, and procedures for litigation-related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for decision on request
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of whether or not to reexamine must be made within 3 months following the filing date of a request. If the 3-month period ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, then the determination must be mailed by the preceding business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should take up a request for decision about 6 weeks after the request was filed. The decision should be mailed within 10 weeks of the filing date of the request. When a reexamination for the same patent has already been ordered and is pending, the examiner should immediately take up the new request (no 6-week delay). (See 35 U.S.C. 303(a) and 37 CFR 1.515(a).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantial new question of patentability is present where there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the prior art patent or printed publication important in deciding whether or not the claim is patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is only necessary that the prior art raise a substantial question as to at least one claim. A 'prima facie' case of unpatentability is not required. SNQ is absent where the same question of patentability has already been decided by a final holding of invalidity after all appeals or by the Office in a previous examination of the patent. Determinations are fact-specific and may be reconsidered by petition or during examination as described in MPEP §2246 and §2248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims considered at time of determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s determination is based on the claims in effect at the time of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments presented with the request by the patent owner in a pending reexamination, amendments in a reissue application on which no reissue patent has been issued, or certain other later-filed claim changes are not to be considered when deciding whether to order reexamination (see 37 CFR 1.515(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statements not considered for ordering decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner claim scope statement and any accompanying information submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) will not be considered by the examiner when making the determination of whether to order ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 301(d) provides that written statements submitted pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 301(a)(2) and additional information under 35 U.S.C. 301(c) are not to be considered by the Office for any purpose other than determining the proper interpretation of a claim in a proceeding ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation search and review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a determination on the request for reexamination, the examiner must request a litigation search from the Technical Support Staff (TSS) of the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) or the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) to check if the patent has been, or is, involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the 'Litigation Review' box on the reexamination IFW file jacket form (RXFILJKT) to indicate the review and its results; scan the litigation search and file jacket form into the IFW reexamination file history. If litigation is or was present and a paper referring to the court proceeding has been filed, reference the paper number in the Litigation Review box. If litigation exists, promptly bring the request to the attention of the CRU Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS) for review to ensure conformity with current Office litigation policy and guidelines (see MPEP §2286).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request content: pertinency and manner requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 302 requires that 'the request must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, the requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of such claims. Failure to set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited art to any claim as required by 37 CFR 1.510(b) can result in no filing date being awarded to the request. See MPEP §§2217 and 2227.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited generally to claims requested
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office’s determination in both the order for reexamination and the examination stage will generally be limited solely to a review of the claim(s) for which reexamination was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is only necessary to establish that a SNQ exists as to one claim to grant reexamination. If the requester did not request reexamination for certain claims, those claims will generally not be reexamined. The Office, however, has discretion to reexamine claims not requested (35 U.S.C. 303(a)) and may do so based on individual facts. Examples (Sony) and MPEP §§2242, 2283 discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or subsequent request standard
rubrics_metrics.description: If a second or subsequent request for ex parte reexamination is filed while a first ex parte reexamination is pending, the grant depends on the prior art cited by the later requester and whether it raises a substantial new question of patentability different from that raised in the pending reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the later request cites the same SNQ as the pending proceeding, the second/subsequent request should be denied. A later request may provide a SNQ as to new or amended claims proposed in the pending reexamination only if it independently provides a different SNQ for the existing claims in effect at the time of determination (37 CFR 1.515(a)). If granted and it appears the request was filed for harassment, a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 may lead to suspension of prosecution on the second/subsequent reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old art may be sole basis post-2002 statutory change
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Law 107-273 (effective November 2, 2002) added that 'The existence of a substantial new question of patentability is not precluded by the fact that a patent or printed publication was previously cited by or to the Office or considered by the Office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliance on 'old art' that was previously cited/considered does not necessarily preclude a SNQ; determinations are fact-specific. Old art may form a SNQ where it is presented/viewed in a new light or with material new argument/interpretation (e.g., claim scope). Use form paragraph 22.01.01 when SNQ is based solely on old art; provide specifics explaining how the old art applies in a new way. See MPEP §2258.01 for use of old art during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior Office decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior favorable decisions by the Office on the same or substantially identical prior art in relation to the same patent generally mean a SNQ is not raised; prior adverse decisions by the Office on the same or substantially identical prior art would usually indicate a SNQ is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should check the patent’s file history to see whether any prior art now advanced was previously cited/considered in an earlier Office examination (including original examination, reissue examination, or earlier reexamination). The weight of decisions in other cases will depend on circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of federal court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A final holding of invalidity or unenforceability by the courts (after all appeals) is controlling on the Office and would preclude the presence of a SNQ as to the claims finally held invalid or unenforceable. Nonfinal (not-yet-final) court holdings are not controlling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Office may accord deference to district court factual findings, the Office makes an independent determination on SNQ because different standards of proof apply. See cited cases (In re Swanson; In re Baxter; Ethicon v. Quigg).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should not reject claims in the order for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on the request for reexamination should discuss all of the patent claims requested for reexamination, but the examiner SHOULD NOT reject claims in the order for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any rejection of the claims will be made in the first Office action on the patentability of the claims issued after the time for submitting any patent owner statement and requester reply that follow the examiner’s order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation and notification of determination
rubrics_metrics.description: A record of the Director’s (or examiner’s) determination will be placed in the official file of the patent, and a copy promptly will be given or mailed to the owner of record and to the person requesting reexamination, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no SNQ is found, a refund of a portion of the reexamination fee may be made to the requester in accordance with 37 CFR 1.26(c). A determination that no SNQ has been raised is final and nonappealable, except by timely petition under 37 CFR 1.181 as provided in 37 CFR 1.515(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard for reexamination ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: In making the determination of whether to order reexamination, the Office will determine the proper meaning of the patent claims by giving the claims their broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification, except in the case of an expired patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For expired patents, claim construction is pursuant to the Phillips standard: words are generally given their ordinary and customary meaning as understood by a person of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention (Phillips v. AWH Corp.). See In re Yamamoto and Ex parte Papst-Motoren citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should indicate initial positions on issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should indicate, insofar as possible, his or her initial position on all the issues identified in the request or by the requester so that comment thereon may be received in the patent owner’s statement and in the requester’s reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps frame the later patent owner statement and requester reply during the reexamination proceeding.
